title: finding(app-shell/studio-design): `ObjectValidationsPanel`'s `conditional` skeleton and editor write the guard as `condition`, which the spec refuses BY NAME in favour of `when` — while the same file promises its skeletons never 422
body:
Measured by the `os-dev` lane delivering PR objectui#9801 (card objectui#9497), and **re-verified on the objectui side by the reviewing seat** — with the spec-side half declared as the lane's reading rather than re-taken, see «Provenance».

## What

`packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectValidationsPanel.tsx` builds a `conditional` rule's skeleton with a guard key named **`condition`**, and its editor reads and writes that same key. The spec spells that rule type's guard **`when`** and refuses `condition` **by name**.

Re-read on objectui `origin/main` by the reviewing seat:

| line | reading |
|---|---|
| `:127`–`:132` | the `conditional` case of the skeleton builder: `condition: 'false'`, plus a nested `then: { type: 'script', …, condition: 'false', … }` |
| `:338`–`:339` | the editor: `value={expressionSource(rule.condition)}` · `onCommit={(cel) => patch({ condition: … })}` |
| `:21` | the file's own summary of the type: *"conditional — a CEL guard + a nested rule applied when it holds."* |

## ⭐ Why it is a contract contradiction rather than a typo

The same file promises the opposite, in its own docblock:

- `:109` — *"A **VALID** minimal skeleton for a rule of `type` — every required field is …"*
- `:24` — *"… skeleton so the immediate object-draft save **never 422s**."*

⇒ adding a conditional rule from the no-code panel produces a draft the object gate **refuses**, on the one path whose stated purpose is that it cannot. That is a reproducible contradiction of a contract the file states about itself, ⛔ not a style question.

## The spec side

Measured by the delivering lane on resolved `@objectstack/spec` **17.4.0**: `ConditionalValidationSchema` spells the guard `when` and rejects `condition` with `unrecognized_keys`, carrying the suggestion *"Did you mean `condition` → `when`?"*.

⚠️ **Provenance, stated rather than blurred:** the objectui readings above are the reviewing seat's own, taken from `origin/main` in the act of filing. The `@objectstack/spec` reading is **the lane's**, ⛔ not re-taken here — this container's `node_modules` is empty, so the reviewing seat cannot resolve the package. ⇒ whoever takes this re-measures the spec half before acting. The suggestion text quoted above is strong evidence the refusal is deliberate and named, but it is a quote of a quote until someone re-runs it.

## Why it was not folded into the card that found it

⛔ Deliberate and correct: objectui#9497 is a **gate** card — nothing lints an object validation rule's predicate at draft level — and this is an **editor writing a wrong key**. Different defect class, different file, and `studio-design/` was outside that branch's surface. ⭐ The two are adjacent in an instructive way: objectui#9497's new gate lints the `when` key, so once both land, this panel's `condition`-keyed guard would be **silently unlinted as well as refused** — the guard the author typed is not the key anything reads.

## Shape of the remedy — ⛔ not decided here

Renaming the skeleton's and the editor's key is mechanical. ⚠️ What is not: whether existing drafts already carry `condition` on a `conditional` rule and need a read-side alias, and whether the panel should surface the spec's own suggestion text rather than silently writing the corrected key. ⛔ Neither was measured.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether any first-party fixture, example or tenant draft already carries a `conditional` rule with a `condition` guard. ⛔ Whether the nested `then` / `otherwise` skeletons have the same mismatch on their own keys — only the outer guard was read. ⛔ Whether any other rule type's skeleton disagrees with the spec's spelling; only `conditional` was examined.

⚠️ Adjacent and correctly **not** filed by the lane: the spec's own `ConditionalValidation` docblock worked examples author `when` with **bare-shorthand** predicates (`account_type = "enterprise"`), the very spelling the server fail-closes on. That is objectstack's published documentation, reached by nothing in objectui.

Refs: objectui#9497 / PR objectui#9801 (the delivery that surfaced it) · objectui#8167 (the editor-scope card next door) · `@objectstack/spec` `ConditionalValidationSchema`.
